mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer savings (RSAFS) signals both tighter monetary policy and reduced household liquidity, which together depress consumer spending and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.3%) in at least 60% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% coincident with a rise in the CPI inflation index of more than 0.4% signals a housing demand shock amid sticky prices, which reduces construction-related earnings and increases cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > -10% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 0.4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (below 1%) combined with a steady or rising CPI inflation index over six months signals accommodative monetary policy in an inflationary environment, which compresses real yields and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL flat or rising for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered regimes.
